title: Kestrel and the Clock
premise: In 1911, in a coastal town on the edge of an empire, apprentice clockmaker Hazel Almeida is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock, only to find the army requisitioning the town and seizing the civic ledger that records every resident's name and origin. Among those now declared enemy is Elias Marchetti, the exiled watchmaker who once taught her her trade and to whom she promised, in peacetime, that she would never let his name be erased. As the master clock becomes the town's official timekeeper for deportations, Hazel hides names inside the clock's mechanism itself, engraving them where no clerk will look. When the requisition order finally reaches her own door, she must choose between fleeing with Elias or staying to keep the clock—and the memory it carries—running; she stays, and the book ends years later with Hazel as the observatory's keeper, winding a clock whose hidden inscriptions have become the town's true record of who belonged.
about_author: C. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a writer of historical fiction who spent a decade restoring antique clocks before turning to fiction full-time. Their work explores how ordinary people preserve truth when institutions rewrite the record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Hazel Almeida, POV: In her master's workshop, Hazel repairs a pocket watch while reflecting that history happens elsewhere, to other people. She is summoned by letter to the observatory: the master clock is failing. Emotional beat: quiet ambition shadowed by her sense of being unimportant, a girl good with her hands and nothing more.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: Before leaving, Hazel visits Elias Marchetti, the aging exile who taught her the trade, and he asks her to carry a message to the observatory's director—an old friend. She promises to remember him, whatever comes. Emotional beat: warmth and unspoken foreboding; the reader senses this promise will cost her.

chapters.title: The Observatory at First Light
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: Arriving at the observatory, Hazel meets Director Voss and begins diagnosing the master clock—a magnificent machine governing the town's official time. She notices the ledger room below, where every resident's name and origin is recorded. Emotional beat: awe curdling into unease as she sees how much power one clock holds.

chapters.title: Soldiers at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: The army arrives without warning, requisitioning the town. Trucks roll through the streets; officers post notices declaring certain surnames enemy. Hazel watches from the observatory steps as neighbors become categories overnight. Emotional beat: shock and denial—her belief that history spares small towns collapses in a single morning.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: Ordered to keep the clock running for military schedules, Hazel glimpses clerks striking names from the ledger—including Marchetti. She copies the page secretly into her notebook. Emotional beat: first act of defiance, trembling and small, but irreversible; invisibility is no longer possible.

chapters.title: What the Clock Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: Cleaning the movement, Hazel discovers previous clockmakers engraved names inside the case—refugees from an older purge, hidden by her predecessors. She realizes the clock has always been an archive. Emotional beat: revelation and inheritance; she understands what her hands are for.

chapters.title: Elias Comes to Town
chapters.summary: Elias Marchetti, POV: Elias arrives seeking Hazel, having learned his name was struck from the ledger. He hides in the observatory's cellar with Voss's reluctant help. Emotional beat: fear braided with tenderness as teacher and student reunite under threat, each protecting the other.

chapters.title: Officer Brandt's Schedule
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: Officer Brandt commandeers the master clock to time deportations precisely, praising its accuracy. Hazel must service it daily under his eye. Emotional beat: humiliation and cold fury—the instrument of her craft turned into an instrument of erasure.

chapters.title: Names in Brass
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: Working nights, Hazel begins engraving the struck names onto brass plates inside the clock's barrel, hidden among the gearing. Elias helps her match handwriting so no pattern shows. Emotional beat: purpose hardening into resolve; grief transmuted into craft.

chapters.title: The Baker's Daughter
chapters.summary: Marta, POV: Marta, a baker's daughter slated for deportation, begs Hazel for help. Hazel can hide her name in brass but not her body. Emotional beat: guilt—the limits of memory-keeping against immediate danger; Hazel learns remembering is not the same as saving.

chapters.title: Voss's Compromise
chapters.summary: Director Voss, POV: Voss, protecting his observatory and his own record, weighs reporting the cellar's occupant. He chooses silence but forbids Hazel further risks. Emotional beat: moral compromise rendered sympathetically; even decent men bargain with survival.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: A senior inspector audits the clock and nearly opens the barrel during maintenance. Hazel improvises a fault to distract him, burning her hand on hot metal to sell the emergency. Emotional beat: terror and adrenaline; the first moment she could die for the names.

chapters.title: The Deportation Train
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: From the observatory gallery, Hazel watches the first train leave, timed by her own repaired clock. Among the crowd she sees Marta board. Emotional beat: devastation; the price of survival made visible, and Hazel's promise transformed into something heavier.

chapters.title: Elias's Confession
chapters.summary: Elias, POV: In the cellar, Elias confesses he was once forced to inform on a friend in another country, and that his exile was penance. He tells Hazel to stop carrying his name if it endangers her. Emotional beat: shame met with forgiveness; Hazel refuses, deepening her commitment.

chapters.title: Brandt Suspects
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: Brandt notices extra tool marks inside the clock and begins watching Hazel, assigning a soldier to shadow her. She plants false evidence implicating a dead clockmaker. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Hazel discovers she can lie well, and hates it.

chapters.title: The Order Reaches Her Door
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: A notice appears: Almeida is also a name on the list. Voss urges her to flee with Elias on a fishing boat leaving in two days. Emotional beat: cornered clarity—staying invisible was never an option; now even flight means abandoning the unfinished names.

chapters.title: Two Days of Wind
chapters.summary: Hazel and Elias, alternating POV: Racing the schedule, they engrave the final names while soldiers search house to house. Voss covers for them one last time, forging maintenance logs. Emotional beat: desperate intimacy and shared purpose; love expressed as labor, side by side in lamplight.

chapters.title: The Night the Clock Stopped
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: To delay the next deportation, Hazel stops the master clock and sabotages the escapement, buying hours. Brandt storms the observatory; Voss takes the blame and is arrested. Emotional beat: climax of sacrifice—the machinery of time itself turned against its masters, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: What Hazel Chose
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: With the boat waiting, Hazel puts Elias aboard and stays behind, surrendering herself to finish the last name and repair the clock before anyone else can. Emotional beat: the book's moral heart—she keeps her promise not by escaping but by remaining; survival and belonging split apart.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: Questioned by Brandt, Hazel claims the engravings are routine maker's marks. The war's end approaches; orders waver; Brandt, facing his own reckoning, lets the matter drop unfinished. Emotional beat: exhausted endurance; justice arrives not as triumph but as bureaucratic fatigue.

chapters.title: The Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: After liberation, the town gathers at the observatory. The clock is opened publicly, the hidden names read aloud, Marta's among them—returned alive. Elias sends word he survived. Emotional beat: catharsis and mourning intertwined; memory restored to the community that erased it.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Clock
chapters.summary: Hazel, POV: Years later, Hazel is the observatory's keeper, training an apprentice of her own. Each winding day she touches the brass names inside the barrel. Emotional beat: resolution and continuity—belonging is not given but kept, like a clock, by hands willing to wind it daily.
